evals.name: dedupe-claude-md-against-readme
evals.prompt: Why does the CLAUDE.md duplicate most of the README.md? I explicitly said not to do this. The README.md is designed for humans, CLAUDE.md is for agents. There shouldn't be any duplication between them. Fix the docs in this project.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md is rewritten so the duplicated Requirements/Usage/Deployment content is removed and replaced with short references to the relevant README sections; the agent-specific Conventions section is retained. README.md keeps its human-facing content, and the generated terraform-docs block is untouched.
expectations: CLAUDE.md no longer contains the duplicated Requirements list, Usage HCL block, or Deployment paragraph verbatim
CLAUDE.md references the README (e.g. 'see README.md') for setup/usage instead of restating it
The Conventions section of CLAUDE.md (locals placement, no jsonencode, fmt/validate/tflint, moved blocks) is preserved
The content between <!-- BEGIN_TF_DOCS --> and <!-- END_TF_DOCS --> in README.md is byte-identical to the original
README.md remains human-oriented and does not gain agent-only conventions

evals.name: drift-check-after-code-change
evals.prompt: I just added a --dry-run flag and support for a SITECHECK_TOKEN environment variable to sitecheck. Does any of the documentation need updating as a result of these changes?
evals.expected_output: Yes — the README documents --depth and --format but not --dry-run or SITECHECK_TOKEN. The README is updated to document both (what --dry-run does, and that SITECHECK_TOKEN enables crawling authenticated pages as a bearer token), and the response states explicitly what was updated.
expectations: The response identifies that --dry-run is missing from the README options list
The response identifies that the SITECHECK_TOKEN environment variable is undocumented
README.md is updated to document the --dry-run flag with an accurate description (lists URLs without fetching)
README.md is updated to document SITECHECK_TOKEN with an accurate description (bearer token for authenticated pages)
The final response explicitly states which files were updated and what changed, rather than silently editing
No CLAUDE.md is created for this change (it is human-facing usage documentation, which belongs in the README)

evals.name: create-docs-with-clean-split
evals.prompt: Review the code in this project and create a README.md and a CLAUDE.md. README.md is primarily for humans. CLAUDE.md is for coding agents. If something is relevant for both, put it in the README.md and reference the relevant section from the CLAUDE.md.
evals.expected_output: A human-oriented README.md (purpose, install, usage of the tagsort CLI including path, --check, the required tag keys, and CI exit-code behaviour) and a short CLAUDE.md that references the README rather than restating it, adding only agent-relevant material (e.g. tooling commands like uv/ruff/pytest). No duplicated paragraphs between the two, no AI-slop tropes, headings in Title Case.
expectations: README.md exists and accurately documents the CLI: the path argument, the --check flag with its CI exit-code behaviour, and the required tag keys (Owner, CostCentre, Environment)
CLAUDE.md exists, references the README for shared information, and contains no paragraph duplicated from the README
No banned trope vocabulary appears in either file (none of: delve, seamless/seamlessly, leverage, robust, comprehensive, cutting-edge, empower, streamline, game-changing)
Neither file contains exclamation marks or a 'Happy coding'-style sign-off
All headings in both files use Title Case
There is no contribution-guide boilerplate section
No claim is made about behaviour the code does not implement (e.g. no invented flags or config files)
